sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (Arab Republic of Egypt) - unitary national jurisdiction; incorporation centrally registered with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - codified civil law system of Napoleonic/French tradition with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution, supplemented by FATF-aligned sectoral AML/CFT regulation and Anglo-American style financial supervisory practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt-United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1992)
Egypt-United Kingdom Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force 1976)
Egypt-UAE Agreement on Investment Promotion and Protection (in force 1999)
Egypt-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1994) reinforced under the Belt and Road investment protection framework
League of Arab States Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980)
Egypt-EU Association Agreement with investment promotion and dispute resolution provisions (2004)

Egypt-UAE Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement and Egypt-UK Double Taxation Convention (1980), in line with Egypt's OECD BEPS Inclusive Framework participation and signature of the BEPS Multilateral Instrument (12 June 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Law No. 181 of 2022, and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 7 of 2003, as amended); Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares and Limited Liability Companies, as amended by Law No. 94 of 2015, and its Executive Regulations as amended by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 152 of 2020 (mandatory beneficial-owner register and GAFI filing obligation); FRA Board Decision No. 97 of 2020 (UBO registration principles); GAFI Decision No. 100 of 2020 (UBO data declaration at incorporation and upon any change in ownership); Central Bank of Egypt Customer Due Diligence AML/CFT Rules; directives and circulars of the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the foreign corporate shareholder (ultimate parent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies or Commercial Registry / Registrar of Companies in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or shareholder resolution of the ultimate parent authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointment of its manager(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate parent company, notarized in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each UBO, director and proposed general manager of the Egyptian LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public or relevant civil registry authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney to the Egyptian formation agent containing signatory and filing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder or board of the ultimate parent, notarized in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Clean criminal record / police clearance certificate of the resident manager(s) and the Arabic-language Articles of Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Residence-country competent authority (police or ministry of interior) for the criminal record; Egyptian Notary Public for the Articles of Association upon execution in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for the foreign criminal record; domestic Egyptian Notary Public attestation for the Articles of Association

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all applicants, UBOs, directors and senior managers against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions Lists (1267/1988/1718 regimes), the Egyptian national asset-freezing list issued under Law No. 80 of 2002 Articles 17-18 and administered by the EMLCU, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the UK OFSI consolidated list where any payment rail or shareholder chain touches the US, EU or UK. PEP identification follows FATF Recommendation 12: verification of name matches, source of funds and source of wealth documentation, senior-management approval before onboarding of any PEP or family member, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. The licensed corporate service provider must retain CDD/EDD records for at least five years after termination of the relationship and file any suspicious transaction report with the EMLCU without tipping off the client.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Investor Portal and Electronic Company Formation Services of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) at https://www.gafi.gov.eg, with name clearance verifiable against the unified Commercial Registry database maintained by the Egyptian Commercial Registry Office and GAFI one-stop-shop service centres
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name must be in the Arabic language pursuant to Law No. 159 of 1981 and its Executive Regulations; the Arabic name constitutes the sole legal name and must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing reserved or registered name in the GAFI registry. A Latin-script transliteration may be recorded as the company's foreign name provided it is a faithful and recognizable transliteration of the Arabic name; phonetic ambiguity, arbitrary abbreviations, and non-standard transliterations are refused. The name must reflect the legal form (limited liability company) and may combine the permissible trade activity with a distinctive trade or family name; names of well-known foreign trademarks are rejected absent a valid trademark licence registered in Egypt.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministry or Authority names already borne by public entities
Names of religions, sects, prophets or ecclesiastical terms contrary to public order
Names of international organizations such as UN, UNESCO, IMF or EU and their Arabic equivalents
Terms identical or deceptively similar to famous trademarks absent a registered licence
Terms contrary to Egyptian public order or morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon issuance of a name rejection notice, the applicant may file a written administrative grievance with the GAFI Complaints and Grievances Committee through the Investor Portal within 30 days of notification, attaching the rejection reference and up to three alternative names; GAFI shall adjudicate the grievance within 15 business days under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Article 83. If the grievance is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Egyptian Administrative Judiciary (State Council) within 60 days of the grievance outcome. Alternatively, where rejection results from trademark conflict, the applicant may submit the prior written consent of the trademark owner together with the Egyptian trademark registration certificate; where rejection results from similarity, the applicant may offer a distinct modified name with a different word order or a supplementary descriptive term and re-file the reservation. All grievance and re-filing procedures are subject to the published GAFI fee schedule.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited - Egyptian law requires the LLC to maintain a real, demonstrable head office address in Egypt evidenced by a certified lease, and that address must appear in the Commercial Registry entry and tax registration. A pure virtual office without any physical presence does not satisfy Law No. 159 of 1981; however, accredited business centres renting a dedicated physical desk or suite within a serviced building are generally accepted for a low-risk online DTC cosmetics business, provided the address is not flagged as a mere letterbox, a nameplate is displayed, and the lease clearly identifies the Registered office suite.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% - quantified medium-low risk. GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Egyptian Tax Authority and the Consumer Protection Agency under Law No. 67 of 2006 may perform unannounced verification visits of registered e-commerce and retail addresses, particularly in serviced-office clusters; maintaining a staffed reception point and orderly statutory records at the registered address materially reduces the probability of an adverse compliance finding.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI name reservation and availability clearance for the proposed Arabic corporate name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory GAFI e-service tariff per the published GAFI fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and authentication of the Arabic Articles of Association and the founding shareholders' resolution before the Egyptian Notary Public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Authority, Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff based on document page count and signature authentication scale

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: GAFI incorporation filing, Commercial Registry registration and issuance of the Companies Register extract for the LLC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) / Commercial Registry Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Capital-based statutory registration fee, capped, per the Companies Law and GAFI prevailing benchmark for a minimal-capital LLC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation summary in the official Egyptian gazette Al-Waqa'i' al-Masriyya and distribution of extracts to the trade register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: National House of Documentation and the official gazette Al-Waqa'i' al-Masriyya
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official gazette publication tariff per column or page set by the House of Documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Arabic translation of foreign corporate and identity documents (certificate of good standing, power of attorney, board resolution, UBO records)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified sworn translator licensed by the Egyptian Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of approximately USD 10-16 per document page, with minimum per-document fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization of the foreign shareholder's corporate documents through the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate in the shareholder's country of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs mission abroad, in coordination with the home-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular tariff of approximately USD 20-50 per document, plus forwarding and agency handling fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) register preparation and initial filing, PEP and UN/OFAC/EU sanctions screening, and AML compliance file set-up

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: GAFI administrative record charge plus prevailing market compliance fee for FATF Recommendations 12 and 24 deliverables

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office for the first year - dedicated physical desk or suite in a serviced business centre in Cairo or Giza accepted as the statutory seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial property operator under Egyptian lease regulations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of approximately USD 70-90 per month for a registered desk in a Grade-B serviced building including reception and mail handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal and paralegal preparation of the formation file, UBO questionnaire, corporate governance charter and Stage 1 due diligence deliverables
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained Egyptian law firm or corporate compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of three to six hours at senior associate rates of USD 90-150 per hour plus fixed document drafting uplift

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 17 of 2019), Articles 1–39 on Limited Liability Companies; Executive Regulations of Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 for GAFI procedures as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Division, Egyptian Ministry of Investment and International Cooperation.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of a Limited Liability Company, filed via GAFI's electronic incorporation portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLC under Law 159/1981; capital must be adequate for the corporate object and fully subscribed. No escrow account is statutorily required, unless the company seeks investment incentives or operates in regulated sectors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporated shareholders subscribe for and be allotted ordinary shares in accordance with the Company's pro forma articles; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [address in Egypt], to which all statutory correspondence and service of process shall be directed; RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Manager and [Name] as Company Secretary, each with authority to execute all filings and open bank accounts; RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorized to engage auditors and commence the Company's corporate registration and tax formalities; and RESOLVED, that this resolution shall take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Electronic Incorporation Portal (Egyptian Companies Online Services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search on GAFI's name reservation system, submit a name reservation application with three alternative names in descending priority, and pay the statutory reservation fee using the founding members' national IDs or passport numbers.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names (primary and alternatives)
National ID cards or valid passports of all founding members
Power of attorney if a legal representative acts on behalf of any member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, GAFI will issue an explicit rejection notice; the applicant may submit a formal administrative objection or re-submit with alternative names, usually resolved within three working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Authentication of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office / GAFI Authentication Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with GAFI's standard LLC template, have all founding partners (or their attorneys-in-fact) sign the document in person before the competent notary, and affix the official authentication stamp. For foreign signatories, a certified power of attorney and passport copies must be notarized at the Egyptian consulate and authenticated by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
required_dossiers: Drafted Memorandum and Articles of Association
Valid national ID or passport of each founder
Power of attorney (if signed by a local representative)
Notarized and consular-stamped foreign documents (for non-Egyptian founders)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies discrepancies or missing attachments, the submission is returned for correction; the applicant may resubmit the same day with the authenticating remarks, and for latent legal defects, seek re-drafting with GAFI's free legal advisory service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with GAFI and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, name reservation certificate, and all supporting identity documents through the GAFI e-portal; automate the payment of filing fees; and await the issuance of the final incorporation certificate. Upon approval, GAFI will register the company in the Commercial Register and publish the notice in the Official Gazette.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Proof of payment of incorporation fees
Identity documents of founders
Fully executed power of attorney (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing content, GAFI issues a deficiency notification; the applicant has ten working days to submit corrective documents through the portal. If the application is formally refused, the company may lodge an administrative appeal with GAFI's Complaint and Grievance Committee, with a decision expected within fifteen working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry and Tax Card Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registry; Egyptian Tax Authority – Central Service Center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the incorporation certificate from GAFI, the manager must register the company in the Commercial Register at the competent office (or the same GAFI portal for one-stop-shop), file the company's original incorporation certificate and lease/ownership contract for the registered office, and apply for a Tax Card at the Egyptian Tax Authority. The Tax Authority will allocate a Tax Identification Number and issue the Tax Card after verifying the registered address and the manager's identity.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Copy of the authenticated Memorandum and Articles of Association
Lease contract or ownership deed of the registered office
Manager's national ID and specimen signature
Confirmation of the corporate bank account (if already opened)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry requests additional supporting evidence or if the Tax Card is withheld, the company may provide the missing lease or address documentation. An administrative appeal may be lodged with the Ministry of Trade and Industry or the Tax Head office; any tax withholding decision may be challenged within 30 days before the Tax Dispute Resolution Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Compliance and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Labor – Social Insurance Authority; Egyptian Civil Defense Administration – Governorate Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Social Insurance Authority as a new entity and enroll any employees within the statutory 30-day window. For the physical storage area, apply to the Governorate Civil Defense Directorate for a fire safety and civil defense clearance, which requires a physical inspection of the office and warehouse premises. Upon passing the inspection, the clearance certificate is issued and must be displayed on the premises.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate
Commercial Registration certificate and tax card
Crisis management plan for the premises
Fire extinguisher maintenance contract
Lease contract, building completion certificate, and structural load compliance certificate
National ID of the manager and the person responsible for safety
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the civil defense inspection flags non-compliance, the company must install required firefighting and safety equipment and re-apply within a 30-day curative window. Non-acceptance can be administratively appealed to the Civil Defense Central Administration, and the clearance process will be closed once remediation is verified.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – online retail of cosmetics does not require an industrial or manufacturing license. The activity is governed by the Trade and Commercial Registration provisions of the Ministry of Trade and Industry, and if a warehouse is operated, a municipal commercial activity license may be required from the local governorate.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; a Commercial Registry desistement for 'E-commerce Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products' and a local governorate warehouse operating licence may be obtained as a supplementary physical activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) – Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA report or registration is mandatory for online retail distribution, unless an on‑site cosmetic mixing/filling line is added. In that case, a risk‑class 'B' environmental registration would be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated. If a warehouse or small packaging room is operated, all solid waste, packaging materials, and damaged cosmetic products must be handled under Law No. 38 of 1994 and its executive regulations, and municipal wastewater discharge must not exceed the thresholds of Law No. 93 of 1962 (as amended).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Governorate Civil Defense Directorate is mandatory for any office/warehouse exceeding minimum area limits; the certificate verifies fire extinguisher placement, emergency exit signage, and alarm system. In addition, a structural load inspection certificate and a workplace healthy-occupancy clearance under Law No. 21 of 1952 must be obtained before employees are allowed to occupy the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – official portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-Taxation services via the unified federal e-invoice and e-filing platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities establishing an Egyptian LLC must complete commercial registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) or the Egyptian Commercial Registry, then obtain a Tax Card from the ETA. The LLC must subsequently register for VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016 via the ETA e-Tax portal. Required documents include the Articles of Association, notarized incorporation forms, legal representative identification, proof of registered office, commercial registration certificate, board resolutions, and bank account details. The ETA issues a unified Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) applicable for corporate income tax, VAT, payroll tax, and stamp duty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt imposes entity-level taxation on LLCs; no check-the-box or general pass-through election exists. Available statutory elections include voluntary VAT registration below the mandatory threshold, appointment of a fiscal representative by non-resident VAT vendors, the small taxpayer simplified taxable base regime under ETA guidelines, and certain election-based transfer pricing documentation reliefs. No hybrid mismatch pass-through election is available under Egyptian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Egyptian VAT Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover; however, any person importing or exporting goods in the course of business is subject to mandatory VAT registration regardless of turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates real-time electronic invoicing (e-invoice) and electronic receipts (e-receipt) through the ETA's integrated clearance platform. Taxpayers must transmit B2B and B2G invoices and credit/debit notes in JSON/XML format via API authentication; each accepted invoice is digitally stamped with a validation code and QR code linked to the ETA real-time fiscal database. Phased enforcement is based on annual turnover thresholds, and non-compliance triggers invoice rejection, tax clearance certificate suspension, and fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods is zero-rated (0% VAT) under Article 19 of the Egyptian VAT Law, provided the goods are physically exported under customs supervision, the supplier holds a valid VAT registration, and the export is completed within the statutory timeline. Certain offshore/intangible services supplied to non-residents may also be zero-rated where the recipient is outside Egypt, the service is actually consumed outside Egypt, and documentary evidence supports the offshore character of the supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Sader/Hawiya) issued by the Egyptian Customs Authority
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Commercially issued export invoice (matching the ETA-validated e-invoice)
Inward Remittance Certificate and/or bank credit confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Valid VAT Tax Card and Export Contract/L/C documentation
Transport evidence (port/container records or CMR) where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA may conduct an export substantiation audit for up to five years, review both inventory and bank submission trails, and retrospectively claw back input VAT offsets together with any uncollected zero-rated output VAT. Penalties include monthly delay tax of 2% on outstanding amounts, an additional fine up to 150% of the tax amount for false export documentation or fraud, and administrative fines up to EGP 50,000 independent of monetary penalties, plus criminal referral for tax evasion under Egyptian tax law. Unjustified export refunds are recoverable with full clawback and compounded penalty interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sovereign monetary authority and foreign-exchange administration acting under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law). The CBE exclusively licenses banks and payment service providers and governs all inward and outward cross-border fund transfers, export-proceeds repatriation, and hedging transactions in Egypt.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains a market-managed floating exchange-rate regime restored by the CBE decision of 6 March 2024, which unified the official and parallel rates and eliminated mandatory forced conversion. Current-account transactions (trade in goods and services) are freely convertible through licensed banks with documentary verification only; no pre-shipment exchange approval is required. Capital-account items (FDI equity injections, shareholder loans, dividend remittances, and branch remittances) are convertible subject to underlying documentation and balance-of-payments registration at the receiving bank. Practical profit-remittance hurdles: (i) dividend remittance requires audited annual financial statements proving distributable reserves, a tax clearance certificate issued by the Egyptian Tax Authority, and settlement of the 10% dividend withholding tax (treaty-reduced rates require a tax residence certificate); (ii) banks will demand proof that the paid-in capital has been reflected in the Commercial Registry and the CBE statistical system before any distribution is processed; (iii) liquidity queues may still arise for USD at smaller banks, but the main institutions (CIB, NBE, Banque Misr) clear legitimate corporate asks within ordinary business days; (iv) all conversions must occur at the published interbank market rate and no parallel-market premium may be recorded in the statutory accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign-exchange instructions issued pursuant to Banking Law No. 194 of 2020, exporters must repatriate and credit the full value of export proceeds to a licensed Egyptian bank within 180 days following the shipping/customs-release date. Historically, 100% of gross export receipts had to be converted into EGP upon receipt; following the 6 March 2024 unified market-rate decision, the mandatory EGP conversion was removed, and exporters may retain proceeds in a foreign-currency export-proceeds account (FCA) and deploy those balances for trade-related foreign-currency payments (supplier imports, logistics, insurance) without prior CBE approval, or convert them at the prevailing interbank rate. The 180-day repatriation deadline remains a hard statutory requirement: any foreign-held balance, including funds resting in digital wallets or offshore EMI accounts, must be physically credited into the Egyptian banking system within that window. Non-compliance exposes the exporter to administrative sanctions, ranging from compulsory conversion at punitive rates, bank-level transaction restrictions, and suspension of the export registration. Extensions are granted only for documented force majeure or carrier delays and require exceptional CBE/account-bank approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution / Escrow Account; operational EGP and USD/export-proceeds FCA
Capital Contribution / Escrow Account; operational EGP and USD/export-proceeds FCA
Operational USD/EGP account; e-commerce merchant-acquiring account; export-proceeds FCA
Operational USD/EGP account; international treasury and MT103/LC corridor
Operational EGP account; trade finance desk for LC / documentary collections
Operational USD/EGP account; FX hedging and treasury counterparty
Operational EGP account; retail-network merchant account and payroll disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Conditional / Medium when used solely as a secondary collection corridor, but Low as a standalone treasury solution. Legal constraints: (i) the CBE export-repatriation regime requires all export proceeds to be credited to a licensed Egyptian bank within 180 days; an offshore digital EMI (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, Modulr) is not a CBE-licensed bank and cannot satisfy the repatriation rule if funds remain abroad; (ii) Egyptian card-network and national payments rules require e-commerce settlement to enter through an Egyptian acquirer or through an Egyptian-licensed payment service provider linked to the local bank account; (iii) Egyptian accounting and tax records must recognise the EMI only as an intermediary, not as a treasury counterparty; (iv) a compliant operating pattern is: PayPal/Shopify settlement → offshore EMI for collection and currency aggregation → immediate onward SWIFT MT103 (within 7 days or less) to the Egyptian beneficiary bank, with the local bank fully notified that the EMI is a mere fronting corridor and with all commercial invoices, shipment proofs, and platform payout statements attached to each remittance; (v) any prolonged accumulation of export proceeds in an offshore wallet is a compliance red flag and will be treated by the Egyptian bank as a breach of the exporter's repatriation undertaking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory. Under Egyptian AML/CFT Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 115 of 2022, and the CBE AML/CFT regulations implemented by licensed banks, first-time corporate account opening requires the physical presence of the legal representatives: the General Manager (or an appointed local director) and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding at least 10% equity or exercising de facto control must attend a face-to-face interview at the bank's branch in Egypt. Remote/video-only onboarding is not accepted for foreign-owned LLCs without a pre-existing banking relationship. In practice, HSBC Egypt and CIB may allow a hybrid arrangement in which the majority foreign UBO executes a notarised and apostilled power of attorney and the local General Manager presents it physically at the branch; nevertheless, the bank's head-office compliance committee will still require the POA's physical submission and a video verification call with the foreign UBO. For foreign-currency and export-proceeds FCA accounts, the file receives an elevated compliance review, often adding three to five business days to the account-activation timetable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore-incorporated intermediate shareholder (e.g., BVI, Cyprus, or UAE holding company) obscuring the ultimate beneficial-owner chain of the Egyptian LLC.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain of title: apostilled certificates of incorporation, register of members, and good-standing certificates for each intermediate entity; UBO declaration identifying all natural persons holding 10% or more or exercising control; certified passport copies and proof of residential address; source-of-wealth evidence for each UBO (sale deeds, audited financial statements, bank reference letters); written corporate rationale confirming the Egyptian LLC operates as the active cosmetics DTC trading entity; and an undertaking to update the UBO register in accordance with Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and the Unified Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket cross-border e-commerce receipts flagged as unexplained or unusual by the bank's Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform KYC dossier consisting of the Shopify store registration certificate, verified website URL, 12 months of PayPal and Shopify Payments payout statements, product catalogue and pricing structure, customer-territory dashboards, refund and chargeback policies; transaction-level commercial invoices cross-matched with shipping evidence (airway bills, customs declarations); audited financials once available; and a board-approved written description of the DTC business model and return/refund flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Real or perceived breach of the 180-day export-repatriation rule because funds are observed accumulating in a Payoneer, Wise, or other offshore wallet before transfer to Egypt.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Historical EMI payout ledger proving that all balances were remitted to the Egyptian bank at least monthly and in all cases well within 180 days; executed SWIFT MT103 advices; inward-remittance advices from the receiving Egyptian bank cross-referenced to shipment dates; an updated export register; and a signed written undertaking to repatriate all export proceeds within 180 days and to provide quarterly cash-pool and wallet-balance reports to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure: customers or suppliers located in OFAC, EU, UN, or CBE-designated jurisdictions, or UBO/PEP ties through nationality, residence, or counterparty relationships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed and signed bank sanctions/PEP questionnaire; geolocation and IP-blocking configuration report for the e-commerce store proving excluded jurisdictions; negative-media screening report; an automated list of prohibited shipping destinations and the platform's technical block settings; certificates of compliance issued by external AML counsel; and a written group AML policy with named compliance officers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-documentation gap for cosmetics imports/exports: absence of product registration or conformity documents creates trade-based money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) cosmetic-product registration certificates or valid exemption confirmations for all imported and exported SKUs; manufacturer free-sale certificates; customs declarations filed through the Nafeza single-window system; commercial invoices; certificates of analysis; and supply contracts with licensed cosmetics manufacturers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Funds may enter Egypt only through an Egyptian-licensed bank using the SWIFT system (MT103 for direct credits; MT202 for treasury interbank legs). The remitting foreign shareholder must be named exactly as in the GAFI investment registration, and the beneficiary must be the LLC's EGP and/or USD capital-contribution account at the onboarding bank. The purpose must be classified as equity capital for direct investment under the BPM6 balance-of-payments code 'Direct Investment – Equity', and the MT103 field 72 narrative must state 'FDI Share Capital under Unified Investment Law No. 72 of 2017'. The Egyptian bank will not credit the capital account until the full compliance file is verified: (i) GAFI investment-registration certificate; (ii) notarised and apostilled Memorandum of Association including the capital schedule and shareholding split; (iii) Commercial Registry extract sealing the managers' authority; (iv) UBO register; (v) sanctions/PEP screening results; and (vi) source-of-funds evidence. After credit, the bank issues an FDI deposit confirmation and registers the inflow in the CBE's electronic balance-of-payments statistics system. The paid-in capital must then be notarised into the MOA within the statutory filing period; in-kind capital contributions are not wired and require a separate bank-approved valuation protocol.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlement: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for supplier prepayments, post-shipment balances, and reimbursement of marketing/logistics services; the paying bank requires the commercial invoice, proforma invoice, underlying contract, and Nafeza customs import entry once goods arrive, and the transfer must be made in the invoice currency without split payments. (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance) issued via SWIFT MT700 are preferred for first-time international suppliers and high-value purchases of packaging and raw materials; payment is made against compliant shipping documents (bill of lading, invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and EDA product registration where applicable). (iii) Documentary collections (documents against payment or acceptance) are suitable for trusted repeat suppliers at lower cost. (iv) Domestic EGP disbursements use the CBE RTGS system and Meeza corporate payment rails. Every outward foreign-currency remittance must be accompanied by the underlying trade documentation and the bank's CBE-mandated FX declaration forms, ensuring consistency with the exporter's balance-of-payments reporting and customs records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP FX forwards with tenors generally up to 12 months, executed under an ISDA/IFXMA master agreement and supported by verified underlying export or import exposure; settlement occurs onshore at the prevailing interbank market rate.
USD/EGP FX swaps combining same-day and forward legs, used for temporary EGP liquidity management and the orderly roll-over of forward positions.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP and EUR/USD/EGP combinations) permitted for medium-term balance-sheet hedging of the LLC's foreign-currency liabilities, including interest-payment legs.

Vanilla USD/EGP foreign-exchange options offered by major private banks (CIB, AAIB, HSBC Egypt), subject to the bank's underlying-trade-exposure test, ISDA documentation, and CBE counterparty limits; premiums may be paid in EGP or USD.

Offshore EGP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not an onshore CBE-permitted product for Egyptian licensed entities; a non-resident parent treasury may execute EGP NDFs offshore strictly for consolidation hedging, but such contracts fall outside the Egyptian regulatory perimeter and are treated as one-way offshore transactions rather than bank-permissible hedging instruments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 2) covering the LLC's taxable profits from online cosmetics and beauty retail, prepared on an accrual basis and reconciled to e-invoicing records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Competent Tax Directorate or Large Taxpayer Center as assigned on the LLC's tax registration certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months of the fiscal year-end; calendar-year LLCs file by 30 April, with the ETA e-filing portal generally accepting submissions through 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay surcharge of 2% per month on unpaid corporate income tax, capped at 100% of the tax due; late-filing administrative fines under the Unified Tax Procedures Law; ETA file lock, enforced collection, and suspension of commercial-registry dealings; persistent non-compliance supports administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement, and notes) prepared under Egyptian Accounting Standards, audited by a licensed certified public accountant, and approved by the General Assembly of members.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) as an annex to the corporate income tax return; a certified copy is retained at the registered office for inspection by GAFI and the Commercial Registry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit completion and General Assembly approval are required before the annual corporate income tax return filing deadline; for calendar-year LLCs, statements must be finalized by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unaudited or unapproved statements forfeit tax deduction defenses; manager personal liability to members arises under the Companies Law; the ETA may issue an estimated tax assessment with the 2% monthly delay surcharge on the additional amount assessed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GAFI company-file maintenance payment and Commercial Registry revalidation confirmation, representing the LLC's annual subscription for continued registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Company Registration and Commercial Registry Directorate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the incorporation anniversary within the Commercial Registry revalidation cycle; GAFI invoices the annual fee at the start of each calendar year for calendar-end entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge on registry fees; suspension of company extracts, commercial certificates, and notarial services; two consecutive years of non-renewal trigger GAFI administrative warnings and deregistration or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership (UBO) register confirmation and updated shareholding declaration identifying the ultimate natural persons behind the LLC's registered members, including any newly transferred member interests.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry within GAFI and competent anti-money-laundering supervisory authorities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any direct or indirect ownership change at or above the 25% disclosure threshold, and no later than the annual Commercial Registry revalidation date for the confirmation cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for incomplete or false UBO disclosures under the anti-money-laundering framework; refusal by notaries to authenticate share transfers; suspension of banking relationships for outdated UBO records; cumulative non-compliance supports administrative removal.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit applies whenever paid-up capital exceeds EGP 50,000 or the number of members exceeds 10 (Companies Law No. 159/1981, Article 124). Even below these thresholds, a licensed auditor is effectively mandatory because the ETA requires audited financial statements in support of the corporate income tax return and the e-audit file.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS; the LLC must maintain double-entry books and preserve e-invoice and e-receipt records for online retail transactions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a current beneficial-ownership register at its registered office and notify the Commercial Registry of any member-level transfer within 30 days where the transfer affects 25% or more of ownership. The annual confirmation cycle reconciles the Register of Members, notarized transfer deeds, and the registered agent's UBO records before the Commercial Registry revalidation date; the same protocol governs changes in the ultimate parent chain above the LLC.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Shareholding Ledger
Minute Book of the General Assembly and Management Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–500 per year for registered-office accommodation, GAFI commercial-registry liaison, and statutory correspondence handling in Cairo.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 700–1,500 per year for the statutory audit of a low-to-mid-volume online cosmetics retail LLC, including preparation of the ETA e-audit file and annual book certification.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for standard online cosmetics retail under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended by Law No. 21 of 2020. Entities licensed within the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) may access a reduced rate (commonly 10%) plus customs and related incentives. Law No. 72 of 2017 provides a 50% investment-cost deduction for qualifying capital-intensive projects, but pure e-commerce retail generally falls outside that classification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tax Form No. 26 (Income Tax Return for Juridical Persons) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal and the ETA 'My Tax' digital platform.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional advance payments are computed on self-assessment projections during the fiscal year, followed by a final annual reconciliation return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed no later than four calendar months after the fiscal year-end (for a 31 December year-end: 30 April; for a 30 June year-end: 31 October), unless an extension is administratively granted by the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from online retail of cosmetics and personal care products, including Shopify and PayPal settlement inflows, translated to EGP at the prevailing exchange rate on the date of receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC reports full Egyptian-sourced commercial income; non-resident shareholders are not required to file a separate Egyptian corporate return merely by reason of their ownership of the LLC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2a-2c (Cost of Sales and Operating Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of imported goods, customs duties, logistics, platform commissions, payment processor fees, rent, salaries, and marketing costs supported by invoices and bank records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are allowed only when arm's length and properly documented; payments to related-party suppliers or licensors require transfer pricing documentation and may be subject to withholding tax at source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule D / Form FM (Transfer Pricing Disclosure)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of related parties, types and amounts of controlled transactions, selected transfer pricing method, and benchmark conclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident related supplier without a permanent establishment in Egypt is not automatically subject to Egyptian CIT, but the related-party transaction must comply with the arm's length standard; the Egyptian buyer must maintain the Local File and attach the disclosure schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7b (Withholding Tax Credits and Treaty Relief)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for Egyptian withholding tax on distributions and interest, plus foreign withholding tax creditable under an applicable double taxation agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty-based reduced withholding requires a valid Egyptian Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership evidence, and prior submission of the DTA relief application through the ETA portal.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Law No. 11 of 2020 (Unified Tax Procedures Law): late filing may trigger a penalty of 5% of the tax due (with a statutory minimum adverse assessment) plus a late-payment surcharge of 2% per month or fraction of a month on the outstanding tax; repeated or wilful non-filing leads to criminal referral, fines up to EGP 50,000, and imprisonment up to five years for evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Egyptian payer must receive, before distribution, a fully completed DTA relief claim form, the payee's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the ETA, and a beneficial ownership declaration; once the ETA acknowledges the claim, the payer applies the reduced treaty rate at source; over-withheld amounts may be reclaimed by filing an ETA refund application.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and on interest paid to non-residents is 20% under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended; most Egyptian DTAs reduce the rate to 10-15%, conditional on treaty residence, beneficial ownership, and economic substance of the recipient.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 for aggregate controlled transactions in a fiscal year; Master File required where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EGP 1,000,000,000; a transfer pricing disclosure schedule is mandatory in all cases where related-party transactions exceed EGP 2,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the ETA invokes substance-over-form, general anti-avoidance rules, and beneficial ownership requirements under Law No. 91 of 2005 as amended; treaty relief and tax planning structures are disregarded where the recipient lacks real economic substance such as premises, personnel, and operational activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of website sales, falsification of e-commerce books, suppression of Shopify and PayPal settlement records, creation of fictitious costs, or fraudulent use of tax exemptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Law No. 91 of 2005 and Law No. 11 of 2020: fine up to EGP 50,000, imprisonment up to five years, and civil collection of the evaded tax plus a penalty of up to 100-150% of the tax due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who sign or approve false returns are jointly and severally liable; ETA may impose asset seizure, travel bans, passport retention, exclusion from public works, and criminal forfeiture of the illicitly suppressed sales proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Round-tripping of cosmetic inventory through a paper intermediary in a low-tax jurisdiction with no employees, office, or operational function, solely to shift profit margins outside Egypt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-recognition of the intermediary, re-characterization of the transactions, upward assessment at the Egyptian 22.5% CIT rate, additional 20% withholding on reclassified royalty or service payments, and late-payment surcharges under Law No. 11 of 2020.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in the artificial structure face personal assessment for the additional tax, director disqualification, travel restrictions, and potential criminal fraud liability if the arrangement is proven to be a sham to mislead the ETA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing consumer payments through foreign PSPs without Egyptian banking on-boarding, failing to identify beneficial owners of large settlements, or allowing the e-commerce platform to be used for money laundering or third-party fund transfers without statutory due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002: imprisonment from three to fifteen years and a fine of EGP 1,000,000-5,000,000; subsidiary sanctions include freezing orders, forfeiture of funds, and suspension or revocation of the commercial registration and e-commerce licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may be personally prosecuted; sanctions include arrest, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and disqualification from serving as directors in Egypt or any other ETA-supervised entity.
